title: Differences between Dataflow Gen1 and Dataflow Gen2 - Microsoft Fabric

claims.text: Dataflow Gen2 is Fabric Data Factory's low-code data preparation item, built on the Power Query experience shared with Excel, Power BI, Power Platform, and Dynamics 365, offering more than 300 transformations over hundreds of source connectors.

Compared with Gen1, Dataflow Gen2 adds multiple output destinations, pipeline integration, high-performance compute, autosave with background publishing, and improved monitoring; Gen1 uniquely retains DirectQuery access through the dataflow connector.

Unlike Gen1, which keeps results in its own internal storage reachable only via the dataflow connector, Gen2 can write transformed output to external and Fabric destinations including Azure SQL Database, Azure Data Explorer, ADLS Gen2, Lakehouse tables and files, Fabric Warehouse, Fabric KQL database, Fabric SQL database, SharePoint files, and Snowflake.

For scale-out query processing, Dataflow Gen2 uses Fabric SQL compute engines and automatically provisions system items named DataflowsStagingLakehouse and DataflowsStagingWarehouse in the workspace; these are internal staging stores not meant for direct user interaction.

Gen2 autosaves edits continuously as a draft, so closing the browser or losing connectivity does not lose work; publishing then persists the dataflow and runs validations in the background rather than blocking the author.
Running Dataflow Gen2 requires a Fabric capacity, a Fabric trial capacity, or a Power BI Premium capacity.

Since April 2026, every new Dataflow Gen2 item is created with CI/CD and Git integration support; the older 'classic' creation path without CI/CD is gone, and existing classic items keep working or can be converted with the Save As feature.

Three migration routes exist from Gen1 to Gen2: exporting queries to a PQT template file and importing them, copying and pasting queries in the Power Query editor, or using Save As to clone any existing dataflow as a CI/CD-enabled Gen2 item in one step.

A common composition pattern is chaining a Dataflow Gen2 with other workloads: load curated data into a lakehouse for notebook analysis, or land data in Azure SQL and let a pipeline move it onward to a warehouse; pipelines can also invoke a dataflow as a scheduled activity.

Copilot in Fabric is integrated into Dataflow Gen2 authoring, letting users connect to sources, apply transformations, generate sample data, and undo steps via natural-language prompts, with each action surfaced as a card plus corresponding applied steps.

Gen2's Recent data module remembers previously used tables, files, folders, databases, and sheets so they can be reloaded onto the canvas without reconfiguring connections, and Browse location lets you pick sibling items from the same folder or database.
